head: 4162bdb1716950415e56e2872f2f40f7e99a955b
classification_reasons: check_ratchets runs at phases (c), (d) and (e) for every change type in every project the plugin drives (intent.md's 'Affected users and systems'): a new, always-on gate check with a wide blast radius, not a localized fix.

The dot-rename-vs-surviving-sibling branch (panel decision #1) is a genuine, non-obvious design choice with a stated evasion risk if read the other way; its correctness depends on documentation (spec/plan/docstring) staying aligned with a dedicated pinning test, which this round's whole arc (three prior escalations) shows is easy to let drift.

Coverage is new, not pre-existing: every behavior this change adds (drop rules, declaration paths, acceptance, skip-marker scan) is proved by tests written in this same change, per plan.md's own interrogation answer 5.
attempted: Intent: this commit's stated goal is narrow (close the last documentation-consistency gap the third review found: plan.md's Proof section missing a dedicated bullet for test_ratchets_eval_case_dot_rename_wins_over_a_surviving_sibling). The diff hunk matches exactly that scope; no scope creep, no reopening of panel decision #1's substantive outcome (left untouched, as instructed).

Spec and plan: re-read spec.md's Requirements (eval-case drop rule, dot-prefixed-rename addition evaluated independently of the survivor rule, citing panel decision #1) and Design (same, with the tree_files/survivor-argument rationale) side by side -- consistent with each other and with the checks.py docstring. Re-read plan.md's Risks section bullet (now names the dot-rename sub-case and the pinning test) and the Proof section: the new bullet `tests/test_gate.py::test_ratchets_eval_case_dot_rename_wins_over_a_surviving_sibling` is now present, immediately after the sibling `test_ratchets_eval_case_partial_delete_is_not_a_drop` bullet, with its own dedicated description matching the test's actual assertion (`details.hits["ratchet: evals"] == ["evals/cases/foo/"]`). No section of plan.md, spec.md or the docstring is left stating or implying a different (or no) rule any more.

Proof: read tests/test_gate.py::test_ratchets_eval_case_dot_rename_wins_over_a_surviving_sibling directly -- it dot-renames one file of a two-file case while the sibling survives, and asserts the whole case is reported dropped; this is a genuine pin of panel decision #1's chosen (fail-closed) behavior, distinct from the single-file dot-rename test and from the partial-delete-is-ok test. Also re-checked dropped_eval_cases's docstring (states the independence 'deliberately', citing panel decision #1) and the pure-function test test_dropped_test_files_and_eval_cases_pure, whose expected output (`["evals/cases/bar/", "evals/cases/baz/"]`) now matches the dot-prefixed-rename case's actual destination path, and the CHECKS_BY_PHASE membership test, which now includes 'ratchets' in its expected check-name set -- both of these were the literal failures the stale gate-c.json recorded from the very first round; neither failure mode is reachable from the code or tests as they stand now. Did not cite or rely on any evidence/claude-*.json, run-c.json, gate-c.json or status.yaml gate record as proof for or against the diff; gate-c.json and status.yaml's parked reason belong to an earlier round in this fix sequence, before this round's fixes were applied.

Blast radius: this commit's own diff touches only plan.md (two bullets: the plugin.json/marketplace.json split noted as already done two rounds back, and the new Proof bullet). No guardrail file (.claude/**, CLAUDE.md, REVIEW.md, sdlc.yaml) is touched by this commit or by the cumulative round diff.

Policies: no security-baseline, data-conventions, coding-standards or definition-of-done rule is implicated by a documentation-only addition; REVIEW.md's own 'Important' definition (would break behavior, leak data or breach a policy) does not reach a missing cross-reference once it is added -- and it is now added.

Tests: the new pinning test is not tautological -- it would fail under the originally-proposed 'filter dot_dropped against survivor_cases' alternative the first-round reviewer wanted, so it genuinely locks panel decision #1's outcome. No existing test was weakened, skipped or deleted this round; the pure-function test's expected value was corrected to match real behavior, not loosened.
